payload.prompt:
Extend the logging hook (no app code changes):

1. In .github/hooks/scripts/log-interaction.js, on the Stop event the payload has
   transcript_path pointing to Copilot's session events.jsonl. When it exists:
   - Read it line by line (JSONL). Keep only: user.message, assistant.message,
     tool.execution_start, tool.execution_complete, permission.requested, permission.completed.

     (overwrite if it exists — Stop can fire more than once per session):
     timestamp + role/type, message text, tool name + short arguments, permission decision.
   - Same redaction; truncate each entry to 2,000 characters with "…[truncated]".
   - Never copy system.message content.
   Put the transcript logic in a function that can also be run manually.

   4da15382-fcfb-4ed1-86dd-8dff609c29ae

Keep everything else unchanged; the hook must still always exit 0 with no stdout. Do not commit.

# Project conventions for AI agents

Invoice approval demo app: ASP.NET Core 8 Web API with a small static web UI.

## Layout

- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Domain`: business rules, no web or storage code. `ApprovalService` owns the invoice lifecycle (Draft, PendingApproval, Approved, Rejected).
- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api`: controllers, sign-in (`Auth/`), in-memory repository, and the web UI under `wwwroot/`.
- `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`: xUnit tests, one test class per class under test, named `<ClassUnderTest>Tests`.
- `e2e`: Playwright end-to-end tests (`tests/`) and page objects (`pages/`).
- `docs/use-cases`: short briefs for features we may build.

## Conventions

- Controllers live in `Controllers/`, one per resource, route `api/[controller]`. Request bodies are `record` types declared inside the controller.
- Controllers inherit `ApiControllerBase` and use `Handle(...)` so service errors map to 404, 409 and 400.
- Every endpoint is behind sign-in. Restrict actions with `[RequireRole("...")]`: destructive actions are Admin only, approvals are Approver or Admin.
- Business rules go in the Domain project, never in controllers.
- Register services in `Program.cs`. Repositories are interfaces in Domain with an in-memory implementation in Api.
- Every new rule or endpoint needs tests. Use `FakeInvoiceRepository` in tests.
- Use clear names; no one-letter variables or `flag` parameters.
- End-to-end tests use page objects and role-based locators (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`), never CSS or XPath selectors.

## Commands

- Run the app: `dotnet run --project backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api` then open http://localhost:5000
- Run the tests: `dotnet test backend/InvoiceApp.sln`
- Run end-to-end tests: `cd e2e && npm install && npx playwright install chromium && npm test`

## Demo accounts (not real credentials)

- `demo.approver` / `ChangeMe123!` (role Approver)
- `demo.admin` / `ChangeMe123!` (role Admin)

## Never

- Commit real credent…[truncated]

name: playwright-e2e
description: Create and run Playwright end-to-end tests for the InvoiceApp web UI. Use for browser workflows, role-based approval scenarios, and regression coverage in e2e/.
---

# Playwright end-to-end tests

## When to use

- A user-facing workflow or API-backed UI behavior needs browser-level verification.
- An approval scenario must be tested from sign-in through its visible result.

## Procedure

1. Put reusable page objects in `e2e/pages/` and test specs in `e2e/tests/`.
2. Use role-based locators only: `getByRole` and `getByLabel`. Do not use CSS selectors, XPath, or fixed sleeps; rely on Playwright's locator assertions and auto-waiting.
3. Use the project's existing `playwright.config.ts`. Its `webServer` starts the API app for the test run; do not start a separate server manually.
4. For the rejected over-limit approval scenario:
   1. Sign in as a Manager using the app's supported test account/setup.
   2. Open an invoice with an amount above 50,000 and record its current status.
   3. Attempt to approve it.
   4. Assert the clear rejection reason is shown and the invoice status remains unchanged.
5. Run the suite with `cd e2e && npm test`.

## Done when

- [ ] Page objects and specs are in their designated folders.
- [ ] Locators use only `getByRole` or `getByLabel`; there are no CSS/XPath selectors or sleeps.
- [ ] The rejected over-limit scenario verifies both the reason and unchanged status.
- [ ] `cd e2e && npm test` passes.

description: Run Stryker mutation testing for InvoiceApp's .NET tests and interpret mutation scores, killed mutants, surviving mutants, and coverage gaps. Use to assess approval-rule test effectiveness before or after a change.
---

# Mutation testing

## When to use

- You need to measure whether tests detect changes to production behavior.
- Approval-rule tests have changed and their effectiveness needs checking.

## Procedure

1. If the global tool is not installed, install the required version: `dotnet tool install -g dotnet-stryker --version 4.13.0`.
2. From `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`, run `dotnet stryker`.
3. Read the generated report for the mutation score, killed mutants, surviving mutants, and mutants with no coverage. Inspect survivors to determine whether a test is missing or the mutant is equivalent.
4. Record each run in [mutation-scores-template.md](./assets/mutation-scores-template.md), marking Run as `before` or `after`. Include the date and concise notes on significant survivors or changes.

## Done when

- [ ] Stryker completed from `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`.
- [ ] Score, killed, survived, and no-coverage counts were read from the report.
- [ ] Results and relevant observations are recorded in the table.

# Approval rule tests

## When to use

- A Domain approval rule is added, changed, or needs stronger regression coverage.
- A blocked approval must be proven not to mutate invoice state.

See [AGENTS.md — Approval limits](../../../AGENTS.md#approval-limits) for the authoritative rules and [AGENTS.md — Testing expectations](../../../AGENTS.md#testing-expectations) for project-wide requirements.

1. Add tests in `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests/ApprovalServiceTests.cs`. Name each test after the rule it proves; use one test per rule.
2. For each threshold or eligibility condition, test a boundary pair: an allowed value and the adjacent blocked value.
3. For **every** blocked case, assert the exact reason, snapshot **all** invoice fields before the attempt, and assert every field is unchanged afterward. Also assert `FakeInvoiceRepository.Update` was called zero times.
4. Use the pattern in [blocked-attempt-test-template.cs](./assets/blocked-attempt-test-template.cs); include every field from the current `Invoice` model in the snapshot.

# [Agent Skills (SKILL.md)](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/agent-skills)

Folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that agents load on-demand for specialized tasks.

## Structure

```
.github/skills/<skill-name>/
├── SKILL.md           # Required (name must match folder)
├── scripts/           # Executable code
├── references/        # Docs loaded as needed
└── assets/            # Templates, boilerplate
```

## Locations

| Path | Scope |
|------|-------|
| `.github/skills/<name>/` | Project |
| `.agents/skills/<name>/` | Project |
| `.claude/skills/<name>/` | Project |
| `~/.copilot/skills/<name>/` | Personal |
| `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | Personal |
| `~/.claude/skills/<name>/` | Personal |

## SKILL.md Format

```yaml
---
name: skill-name              # Required: 1-64 chars, lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens, must match folder
description: 'What and when to use. Max 1024 chars.'
argument-hint: 'Optional hint shown for slash invocation'
user-invocable: true          # Optional: show as slash command (default: true)
disable-model-invocation: false # Optional: disable automatic model-triggered loading
---
```

### Body

- What the skill accomplishes
- When to use (triggers and use cases)
- Step-by-step procedures
- References to resources: `[script](./scripts/test.js)`

## Template

```markdown
---
name: webapp-testing
description: 'Test web applications using Playwright. Use for verifying frontend, debugging UI, capturing screenshots.'
---

# Web Application Testing

## When to Use
- Verify frontend functionality
- Debug UI behavior

## Procedure
1. Start the web server
2. Run [test script](./scripts/test.js)
3. Review screenshots in `./screenshots/`
```

## Progressive Loading

1. **Discovery** (~100 tokens): Agent reads `name` and `description`
2. **Instructions** (<5000 tokens): Loads `SKILL.md` body when relevant
3. **Resources**: Additional files load only when referenced

Keep file references one level deep from `SKILL.md`.

# Project conventions for AI agents

Invoice approval demo app: ASP.NET Core 8 Web API with a small static web UI.

## Layout

- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Domain`: business rules, no web or storage code. `ApprovalService` owns the invoice lifecycle (Draft, PendingApproval, Approved, Rejected).
- Approval-limit rules live in Domain (`ApprovalService` or a dedicated policy class). The API gets the approver's role from the session and passes it into Domain; Domain must never read HTTP or session state.
- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api`: controllers, sign-in (`Auth/`), in-memory repository, and the web UI under `wwwroot/`.
- `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`: xUnit tests, one test class per class under test, named `<ClassUnderTest>Tests`.
- `e2e`: Playwright end-to-end tests (`tests/`) and page objects (`pages/`).
- `docs/use-cases`: short briefs for features we may build.

## Approval limits (feature on branch feature/approval-limits)

- Only Manager and Director may approve; Admin retains admin rights but cannot approve.
- Manager may approve up to and including 50,000.00. Director may approve alone up to and including 500,000.00.
- Above 500,000.00 requires two distinct approvers: the first may be a Manager or Director; the second must be a Director.
- Negative rule 1: the same user can never count as both approvers; compare usernames case-insensitively.
- Negative rule 2: a blocked attempt must return a clear reason and change nothing: no status, approver, first approval, timestamp, or repository `Update` call. Throw a dedicated Domain exception; `ApiControllerBase` maps it to 403 Forbidden.
- Amounts are `decimal`; never use `float` or `double` for money.
- Repositories return the same object reference from `GetById`, and `FakeInvoiceRepository.Update` is a no-op. Validate everything before mutating; snapshot every invoice field in blocked-attempt tests and assert none changed.

# [Custom Agents (.agent.md)](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/custom-agents)

Custom personas with specific tools, instructions, and behaviors. Use for orchestrated workflows with role-based tool restrictions.

## Locations

| Path | Scope |
|------|-------|
| `.github/agents/*.agent.md` | Workspace |
| `<profile>/agents/*.agent.md` | User profile |

## Frontmatter

```yaml
---
description: "<required>"    # For agent picker and subagent discovery
name: "Agent Name"           # Optional, defaults to filename
tools: [search, web]         # Optional: aliases, MCP (<server>/*), extension tools
model: "Claude Sonnet 4"     # Optional, uses picker default; supports array for fallback
reasoning-effort: "high"     # Optional: low, medium, high, xhigh, or max
argument-hint: "Task..."     # Optional, input guidance
agents: [agent1, agent2]     # Optional, restrict allowed subagents by name (omit = all, [] = none)
user-invocable: true         # Optional, show in agent picker (default: true)
disable-model-invocation: false  # Optional, prevent subagent invocation (default: false)
handoffs: [...]              # Optional, transitions to other agents
hooks:                       # Optional, inline hooks for this agent's lifecycle events
  PreToolUse:
    - type: command
      command: "./scripts/validate.sh"
  PostToolUse:
    - type: command
      command: "./scripts/format.sh"
---
```

### Invocation Control

| Attribute | Default | Effect |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| `user-invocable: false` | `true` | Hide from agent picker, only accessible as subagent |
| `disable-model-invocation: true` | `false` | Prevent other agents from invoking as subagent |

### Model Fallback

```yaml
model: ['Claude Sonnet 4.5 (copilot)', 'GPT-5 (copilot)']  # First available model is used
```

### Reasoning Effort

Use `reasoning-effort` to set the reasoning level for the custom agent's model:

```yaml
reasoning-effort: high  # low, medium, high, xhigh, or max
```

# Playwright end-to-end tests

## When to use

- A user-facing workflow or API-backed UI behavior needs browser-level verification.
- An approval scenario must be tested from sign-in through its visible result.

## Procedure

1. Put reusable page objects in `e2e/pages/` and test specs in `e2e/tests/`.
2. Use role-based locators only: `getByRole` and `getByLabel`. Do not use CSS selectors, XPath, or fixed sleeps; rely on Playwright's locator assertions and auto-waiting.
3. Use the project's existing `playwright.config.ts`. Its `webServer` starts the API app for the test run; do not start a separate server manually.
4. For the rejected over-limit approval scenario:
   1. Sign in using the app's supported test account/setup and create an invoice through the UI with an amount above 50,000 (for example, 50,001).
   2. Submit the invoice for approval through the UI.
   3. Sign in as a Manager, open the submitted invoice, and record its current status.
   4. Attempt to approve it.
   5. Assert the clear rejection reason is shown and the invoice status remains unchanged.
5. Run the suite with `cd e2e && npm test`.

- [ ] Page objects and specs are in their designated folders.
- [ ] Locators use only `getByRole` or `getByLabel`; there are no CSS/XPath selectors or sleeps.
- [ ] The rejected over-limit scenario verifies both the reason and unchanged status.
- [ ] `cd e2e && npm test` passes.

- A Domain approval rule is added, changed, or needs stronger regression coverage.

1. Add tests in `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests/ApprovalServiceTests.cs`. Name each test after the rule it proves; use one test per rule.
2. For each threshold or eligibility condition, test a boundary pair: an allowed value and the adjacent blocked value.
3. For **every** blocked case, assert the exact reason, snapshot **all** invoice fields before the attempt, and assert every field is unchanged afterward. Also assert `FakeInvoiceRepository.Update` was called zero times.
4. Use the pattern in [blocked-attempt-test-template.cs](./assets/blocked-attempt-test-template.cs); include every field from the current `Invoice` model in the snapshot.
5. Cover both negative rules explicitly. For the same-user rule, test an identical username and one differing only by letter case. For each blocked attempt, prove nothing changed using step 3. After a blocked same-user second approval, assert the first approval is still recorded unchanged and that a different Director can still complete the approval.
6. Assert concrete outcomes and reasons. Never write a test that only asserts “no exception.”
7. Run `dotnet test backend/InvoiceApp.sln` and confirm the new tests pass.

## Done when

# PR review verdicts

## When to use

- Reviewing a change that affects invoice approval, its API integration, tests, or related files.
- Recording actionable review findings and their final disposition.

## Procedure

1. Read [AGENTS.md — Approval limits](../../../AGENTS.md#approval-limits) and [AGENTS.md — Review expectations](../../../AGENTS.md#review-expectations). Treat AGENTS.md as the source of truth.
2. Check the change against this checklist:
   - [ ] Approval behavior matches AGENTS.md.
   - [ ] Both negative rules are enforced and tested.
   - [ ] All conditions are validated before invoice mutation.
   - [ ] The dedicated Domain exception maps to HTTP 403.
   - [ ] Each rule has meaningful tests, including blocked-state assertions.
   - [ ] Changes stay within scope; no unrelated refactors.
3. For each issue, record severity (`critical`, `major`, `minor`, or `trivial`), `file:line`, the finding, and a suggested fix. Use [review-findings-template.md](./assets/review-findings-template.md).
4. Give **every** finding exactly one verdict: `fixed`, `dismissed`, or `deferred`. For dismissed or deferred findings, state the reason. Do not leave a finding without a verdict.
5. Re-check any fix against the checklist and confirm the recorded verdict and reason accurately reflect the final state.

## Done when

- [ ] The full checklist has been considered against the change.
- [ ] Every finding has a severity, file:line, suggested fix, verdict, and applicable reason.
- [ ] Fixed, dismissed, and deferred outcomes are clearly distinguished.

---
name: mutation-testing
description: Run Stryker mutation testing for InvoiceApp's .NET tests and interpret mutation scores, killed mutants, surviving mutants, and coverage gaps. Use to assess approval-rule test effectiveness before or after a change.
---

# Mutation testing

## When to use

- You need to measure whether tests detect changes to production behavior.
- Approval-rule tests have changed and their effectiveness needs checking.

## Procedure

1. If the global tool is not installed, install the required version: `dotnet tool install -g dotnet-stryker --version 4.13.0`.
2. From `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`, run `dotnet stryker`.
3. Read the generated report for the mutation score, killed mutants, surviving mutants, and mutants with no coverage. Inspect survivors to determine whether a test is missing or the mutant is equivalent.
4. Record each run in the **Mutation scores** table in [ASSIGNMENT.md](../../../ASSIGNMENT.md) at the repository root, marking Run as `before` or `after`. Include the date and concise notes on significant survivors or changes. If the file or table is missing, create the table from [mutation-scores-template.md](./assets/mutation-scores-template.md); never edit the template file itself.

## Done when

- [ ] Stryker completed from `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`.
- [ ] Score, killed, survived, and no-coverage counts were read from the report.
- [ ] Results and relevant observations are recorded in the table.

# [Custom Agents (.agent.md)](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/custom-agents)

Custom personas with specific tools, instructions, and behaviors. Use for orchestrated workflows with role-based tool restrictions.

## Locations

| Path | Scope |
|------|-------|

```yaml
---
description: "<required>"    # For agent picker and subagent discovery
name: "Agent Name"           # Optional, defaults to filename
tools: [search, web]         # Optional: aliases, MCP (<server>/*), extension tools
model: "Claude Sonnet 4"     # Optional, uses picker default; supports array for fallback
reasoning-effort: "high"     # Optional: low, medium, high, xhigh, or max
argument-hint: "Task..."     # Optional, input guidance
agents: [agent1, agent2]     # Optional, restrict allowed subagents by name (omit = all, [] = none)
user-invocable: true         # Optional, show in agent picker (default: true)
disable-model-invocation: false  # Optional, prevent subagent invocation (default: false)
handoffs: [...]              # Optional, transitions to other agents
hooks:                       # Optional, inline hooks for this agent's lifecycle events
  PreToolUse:
    - type: command

  PostToolUse:
    - type: command
      command: "./scripts/format.sh"
---
```

| Attribute | Default | Effect |
|-----------|---------|--------|

model: ['Claude Sonnet 4.5 (copilot)', 'GPT-5 (copilot)']  # First available model is used
```

### Reasoning Effort

Use `reasoning-effort` to set the reasoning level for the custom agent's model:

```yaml
reasoning-effort: high  # low, medium, high, xhigh, or max
```

Folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that agents load on-demand for specialized tasks.

## Structure

```
.github/skills/<skill-name>/

| Path | Scope |
|------|-------|
| `.github/skills/<name>/` | Project |
| `.agents/skills/<name>/` | Project |
| `.claude/skills/<name>/` | Project |
| `~/.copilot/skills/<name>/` | Personal |
| `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | Personal |
| `~/.claude/skills/<name>/` | Personal |

## SKILL.md Format

```yaml
---
name: skill-name              # Required: 1-64 chars, lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens, must match folder
description: 'What and when to use. Max 1024 chars.'
argument-hint: 'Optional hint shown for slash invocation'
user-invocable: true          # Optional: show as slash command (default: true)
disable-model-invocation: false # Optional: disable automatic model-triggered loading
---
```

- What the skill accomplishes
- When to use (triggers and use cases)
- Step-by-step procedures
- References to resources: `[script](./scripts/test.js)`

---
name: webapp-testing
description: 'Test web applications using Playwright. Use for verifying frontend, debugging UI, capturing screenshots.'
---

- Verify frontend functionality

# Project conventions for AI agents

Invoice approval demo app: ASP.NET Core 8 Web API with a small static web UI.

## Layout

- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Domain`: business rules, no web or storage code. `ApprovalService` owns the invoice lifecycle (Draft, PendingApproval, Approved, Rejected).
- Approval-limit rules live in Domain (`ApprovalService` or a dedicated policy class). The API gets the approver's role from the session and passes it into Domain; Domain must never read HTTP or session state.
- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api`: controllers, sign-in (`Auth/`), in-memory repository, and the web UI under `wwwroot/`.
- `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`: xUnit tests, one test class per class under test, named `<ClassUnderTest>Tests`.
- `e2e`: Playwright end-to-end tests (`tests/`) and page objects (`pages/`).
- `docs/use-cases`: short briefs for features we may build.

## Approval limits (feature on branch feature/approval-limits)

- Only Manager and Director may approve; Admin retains admin rights but cannot approve.
- Manager may approve up to and including 50,000.00. Director may approve alone up to and including 500,000.00.
- Above 500,000.00 requires two distinct approvers: the first may be a Manager or Director; the second must be a Director.
- Negative rule 1: the same user can never count as both approvers; compare usernames case-insensitively.
- Negative rule 2: a blocked attempt must return a clear reason and change nothing: no status, approver, first approval, timestamp, or repository `Update` call. Throw a dedicated Domain exception; `ApiControllerBase` maps it to 403 Forbidden.
- Amounts are `decimal`; never use `float` or `double` for money.
- Repositories return the same object reference from `GetById`, and `FakeInvoiceRepository.Update` is a no-op. Validate everything before mutating; snapshot every invoice field in blocked-attempt tests and assert none changed.

# [Hooks (.json)](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/hooks)

Deterministic lifecycle automation for agent sessions. Use hooks to enforce policy, automate validation, and inject runtime context.

## Locations

| Path | Scope |
|------|-------|
| `.github/hooks/*.json` | Workspace (team-shared) |
| `.claude/settings.local.json` | Workspace local (not committed) |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Workspace |
| `~/.claude/settings.json` | User profile |

Hooks from all configured locations are collected and executed; workspace and user hooks do not override each other.

## Hook Events

| Event | Trigger |
|------|-------|
| `SessionStart` | First prompt of a new agent session |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | User submits a prompt |
| `PreToolUse` | Before tool invocation |
| `PostToolUse` | After successful tool invocation |
| `PreCompact` | Before context compaction |
| `SubagentStart` | Subagent starts |
| `SubagentStop` | Subagent ends |
| `Stop` | Agent session ends |

## Configuration Format

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "type": "command",
        "command": "./scripts/validate-tool.sh",
        "timeout": 15
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Each hook command supports:
- `type` (must be `command`)
- `command` (default)
- `windows`, `linux`, `osx` (platform overrides)
- `cwd`, `env`, `timeout`

## Input / Output Contract

Hooks receive JSON on stdin and can return JSON on stdout.

- Common output: `continue`, `stopReason`, `systemMessage`
- `PreToolUse` permissions are read from `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision` (`allow` | `ask` | `deny`)
- `PostToolUse` output can block further processing with `decision: block`

`PreToolUse` example output:

```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
    "permissionDecision": "ask",
    "permissionDecisionReason": "Needs user confirmation"
  }
}
```

Exit codes:
- `0` success
- `2` blocking error
- Other values produce non-blocking warnings

# [Custom Agents (.agent.md)](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/custom-agents)

Custom personas with specific tools, instructions, and behaviors. Use for orchestrated workflows with role-based tool restrictions.

## Locations

| Path | Scope |
|------|-------|
| `.github/agents/*.agent.md` | Workspace |
| `<profile>/agents/*.agent.md` | User profile |

## Frontmatter

```yaml
---
description: "<required>"    # For agent picker and subagent discovery
name: "Agent Name"           # Optional, defaults to filename
tools: [search, web]         # Optional: aliases, MCP (<server>/*), extension tools
model: "Claude Sonnet 4"     # Optional, uses picker default; supports array for fallback
reasoning-effort: "high"     # Optional: low, medium, high, xhigh, or max
argument-hint: "Task..."     # Optional, input guidance
agents: [agent1, agent2]     # Optional, restrict allowed subagents by name (omit = all, [] = none)
user-invocable: true         # Optional, show in agent picker (default: true)
disable-model-invocation: false  # Optional, prevent subagent invocation (default: false)
handoffs: [...]              # Optional, transitions to other agents
hooks:                       # Optional, inline hooks for this agent's lifecycle events
  PreToolUse:
    - type: command
      command: "./scripts/validate.sh"
  PostToolUse:
    - type: command
      command: "./scripts/format.sh"
---
```

### Invocation Control

| Attribute | Default | Effect |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| `user-invocable: false` | `true` | Hide from agent picker, only accessible as subagent |
| `disable-model-invocation: true` | `false` | Prevent other agents from invoking as subagent |

### Model Fallback

```yaml
model: ['Claude Sonnet 4.5 (copilot)', 'GPT-5 (copilot)']  # First available model is used
```

### Reasoning Effort

Use `reasoning-effort` to set the reasoning level for the custom agent's model:

```yaml
reasoning-effort: high  # low, medium, high, xhigh, or max
```

# Project conventions for AI agents

Invoice approval demo app: ASP.NET Core 8 Web API with a small static web UI.

## Layout

- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Domain`: business rules, no web or storage code. `ApprovalService` owns the invoice lifecycle (Draft, PendingApproval, Approved, Rejected).
- Approval-limit rules live in Domain (`ApprovalService` or a dedicated policy class). The API gets the approver's role from the session and passes it into Domain; Domain must never read HTTP or session state.
- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api`: controllers, sign-in (`Auth/`), in-memory repository, and the web UI under `wwwroot/`.
- `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`: xUnit tests, one test class per class under test, named `<ClassUnderTest>Tests`.
- `e2e`: Playwright end-to-end tests (`tests/`) and page objects (`pages/`).
- `docs/use-cases`: short briefs for features we may build.

## Approval limits (feature on branch feature/approval-limits)

- Only Manager and Director may approve; Admin retains admin rights but cannot approve.
- Manager may approve up to and including 50,000.00. Director may approve alone up to and including 500,000.00.
- Above 500,000.00 requires two distinct approvers: the first may be a Manager or Director; the second must be a Director.
- Negative rule 1: the same user can never count as both approvers; compare usernames case-insensitively.
- Negative rule 2: a blocked attempt must return a clear reason and change nothing: no status, approver, first approval, timestamp, or repository `Update` call. Throw a dedicated Domain exception; `ApiControllerBase` maps it to 403 Forbidden.

# [Hooks (.json)](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/hooks)

Deterministic lifecycle automation for agent sessions. Use hooks to enforce policy, automate validation, and inject runtime context.

## Locations

| Path | Scope |
|------|-------|
| `.github/hooks/*.json` | Workspace (team-shared) |
| `.claude/settings.local.json` | Workspace local (not committed) |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Workspace |
| `~/.claude/settings.json` | User profile |

Hooks from all configured locations are collected and executed; workspace and user hooks do not override each other.

## Hook Events

| Event | Trigger |
|------|-------|
| `SessionStart` | First prompt of a new agent session |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | User submits a prompt |
| `PreToolUse` | Before tool invocation |
| `PostToolUse` | After successful tool invocation |
| `PreCompact` | Before context compaction |
| `SubagentStart` | Subagent starts |
| `SubagentStop` | Subagent ends |
| `Stop` | Agent session ends |

## Configuration Format

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "type": "command",
        "command": "./scripts/validate-tool.sh",
        "timeout": 15
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Each hook command supports:
- `type` (must be `command`)
- `command` (default)
- `windows`, `linux`, `osx` (platform overrides)
- `cwd`, `env`, `timeout`

## Input / Output Contract

Hooks receive JSON on stdin and can return JSON on stdout.

- Common output: `continue`, `stopReason`, `systemMessage`
- `PreToolUse` permissions are read from `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision` (`allow` | `ask` | `deny`)
- `PostToolUse` output can block further processing with `decision: block`

`PreToolUse` example output:

```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
    "permissionDecision": "ask",
    "permissionDecisionReason": "Needs user confirmation"
  }
}
```

Exit codes:
- `0` success
- `2` blocking error
- Other values produce non-blocking warnings

Invoice approval demo app: ASP.NET Core 8 Web API with a small static web UI.

## Layout

- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Domain`: business rules, no web or storage code. `ApprovalService` owns the invoice lifecycle (Draft, PendingApproval, Approved, Rejected).

- `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`: xUnit tests, one test class per class under test, named `<ClassUnderTest>Tests`.
- `e2e`: Playwright end-to-end tests (`tests/`) and page objects (`pages/`).

- Above 500,000.00 requires two distinct approvers: the first may be a Manager or Director; the second must be a Director.
- Negative rule 1: the same user can never count as both approvers; compare usernames case-insensitively.

- Repositories return the same object reference from `GetById`, and `FakeInvoiceRepository.Update` is a no-op. Validate everything before mutating; snapshot every invoice field in blocked-attempt tests and assert none changed.

# Playwright end-to-end tests

## When to use

- A user-facing workflow or API-backed UI behavior needs browser-level verification.
- An approval scenario must be tested from sign-in through its visible result.

## Procedure

1. Put reusable page objects in `e2e/pages/` and test specs in `e2e/tests/`.
2. Use role-based locators only: `getByRole` and `getByLabel`. Do not use CSS selectors, XPath, or fixed sleeps; rely on Playwright's locator assertions and auto-waiting.
3. Use the project's existing `playwright.config.ts`. Its `webServer` starts the API app for the test run; do not start a separate server manually.
4. For the rejected over-limit approval scenario:
   1. Sign in using the app's supported test account/setup and create an invoice through the UI with an amount above 50,000 (for example, 50,001).
   2. Submit the invoice for approval through the UI.
   3. Sign in as a Manager, open the submitted invoice, and record its current status.
   4. Attempt to approve it.
   5. Assert the clear rejection reason is shown and the invoice status remains unchanged.
5. Run the suite with `cd e2e && npm test`.

## Done when

- [ ] Page objects and specs are in their designated folders.
- [ ] Locators use only `getByRole` or `getByLabel`; there are no CSS/XPath selectors or sleeps.
- [ ] The rejected over-limit scenario verifies both the reason and unchanged status.
- [ ] `cd e2e && npm test` passes.

# UC-2: Partial approval


## Background

Today an invoice is approved or rejected as a whole. Two school districts asked for a way to approve less than the full amount when part of an invoice is disputed.

## The change

An approver can approve an invoice for an amount lower than the invoiced amount, with a required note explaining why.

## What the business asked for

- The approver enters the approved amount, which must be greater than zero and less than the invoiced amount.
- Both the invoiced amount and the approved amount are kept on the invoice.
- The invoice shows as partially approved, separate from fully approved.
- A note is required whenever the approved amount is lower than the invoiced amount.
- Existing approve and reject behaviour stays exactly as it is.

## Where it touches the code

The existing approval flow: `ApprovalService`, `ApprovalsController`, and the Approvals tab in the web UI.

# [Hooks (.json)](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/hooks)

Deterministic lifecycle automation for agent sessions. Use hooks to enforce policy, automate validation, and inject runtime context.

## Locations

| Path | Scope |
|------|-------|
| `.github/hooks/*.json` | Workspace (team-shared) |
| `.claude/settings.local.json` | Workspace local (not committed) |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Workspace |
| `~/.claude/settings.json` | User profile |

Hooks from all configured locations are collected and executed; workspace and user hooks do not override each other.

## Hook Events

| Event | Trigger |
|------|-------|
| `SessionStart` | First prompt of a new agent session |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | User submits a prompt |
| `PreToolUse` | Before tool invocation |
| `PostToolUse` | After successful tool invocation |
| `PreCompact` | Before context compaction |
| `SubagentStart` | Subagent starts |
| `SubagentStop` | Subagent ends |
| `Stop` | Agent session ends |

## Configuration Format

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "type": "command",
        "command": "./scripts/validate-tool.sh",
        "timeout": 15
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Each hook command supports:
- `type` (must be `command`)
- `command` (default)
- `windows`, `linux`, `osx` (platform overrides)
- `cwd`, `env`, `timeout`

## Input / Output Contract

Hooks receive JSON on stdin and can return JSON on stdout.

- Common output: `continue`, `stopReason`, `systemMessage`
- `PreToolUse` permissions are read from `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision` (`allow` | `ask` | `deny`)
- `PostToolUse` output can block further processing with `decision: block`

`PreToolUse` example output:

```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
    "permissionDecision": "ask",
    "permissionDecisionReason": "Needs user confirmation"
  }
}
```

Exit codes:
- `0` success
- `2` blocking error
- Other values produce non-blocking warnings

# Hooks for GitHub Copilot

Run your own checks, logging, or other commands at defined points while a Copilot agent works.

## What are hooks?

Hooks are a way of executing custom shell commands at strategic points in an agent's workflow, such as when an agent session starts or ends, when you enter a prompt, or when a tool is called.

Hooks receive detailed information about agent actions via JSON input, enabling context-aware automation. For example, you can use hooks to:

* Programmatically approve or deny tool executions.
* Use built-in security features like secret scanning to prevent credential leaks.
* Implement custom validation rules and audit logging for compliance.

Unlike custom instructions, hooks run code rather than asking the model to follow a rule. For example, a hook can run a script that checks a tool request before it executes.

## Where you can use hooks

Hooks are available in:

* **The GitHub Copilot app**, which supports repository hooks and hooks supplied by plugins. See [Customizing the GitHub Copilot app](/en/copilot/how-tos/github-copilot-app/customize-github-copilot-app).
* **GitHub Copilot CLI**, where commands run in its execution environment.
* **Copilot cloud agent**, where commands run in the agent's cloud environment. Only a subset of events is supported.
* **Visual Studio Code**, where the hooks experience is in public preview. Supported events and configuration depend on the agent running the session. See [Agent hooks in VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/hooks).

The configuration and examples below describe hooks for Copilot CLI and Copilot cloud agent. Do not assume that the same events, input, or output work unchanged across surfaces.

Run automated checks—like linting, formatting, or security scans—at key points during agent execution to enforce quality standards.

Hooks allow you to extend and customize the behavior of GitHub Copilot agents by executing custom shell commands at key points during agent execution. For a conceptual overview of hooks—including details of the available hook triggers—see [About hooks for GitHub Copilot](/en/copilot/concepts/agents/hooks).

## Creating a hook in a repository on GitHub

1. Create a new `NAME.json` file (where `NAME` describes the purpose of the file) in the `.github/hooks/` folder of your repository.

   > \[!IMPORTANT]
   > The hooks configuration file **must be present** on your repository's default branch to be used by Copilot cloud agent.

2. In your text editor, copy and paste the following hook template. Remove any hooks you don't plan on using from the `hooks` array.

   ```json copy
   {
     "version": 1,
     "hooks": {
       "sessionStart": [...],
       "sessionEnd": [...],
       "userPromptSubmitted": [...],
       "preToolUse": [...],
       "postToolUse": [...],
       "errorOccurred": [...]
     }
   }
   ```

3. Configure your hook syntax under the `bash` and `powershell` keys, or directly reference script files you have created.

   > \[!NOTE]
   > Include both a `bash` key (with a script for Linux and macOS) and a `powershell` key (for a script for Windows) to allow the hooks to run on all three operating systems. Copilot uses the appropriate key based on the user's operating system.

   * This example runs a script that outputs the start date of the session to a log file using the `sessionStart` hook:

       {

         "bash": "echo \"Session started: $(date)\" >> logs/session.log",

Find hook events, configuration formats, and input payloads for hooks in Copilot CLI and Copilot cloud agent.

## Introduction

Hooks are external commands that execute at specific lifecycle points during a session, enabling custom automation, security controls, and integrations.

Hooks are supported in two Copilot surfaces: Copilot CLI and Copilot cloud agent. Most of the configuration fo

## `SubagentStop`

The `SubagentStop` hook fires when a subagent is about to stop.

### Input

In addition to the [common input](about:blank#_common-input), the hook receives:

```
{  "agent_id": "subagent-456",  "agent_type": "Plan",  "stop_hook_active": false}
```

| Field              | Type    | Description                                                                                       |
| ------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `agent_id`         | string  | Identifier for the subagent.                                                                      |
| `agent_type`       | string  | Agent name, such as `"Plan"` or a custom agent name.                                              |
| `stop_hook_active` | boolean | `true` when the subagent is already continuing because a previous `SubagentStop` hook blocked it. |

### Output

The hook can require the subagent to continue:

```
{  "decision": "block",  "reason": "Verify the results before completing."}
```

| Field      | Values or type | Description                                                                       |
| ---------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `decision` | `"block"`      | Prevents the subagent from stopping.                                              |
| `reason`   | string         | Required when `decision` is `"block"`. Explains why the subagent should continue. |

## `SubagentStop`

The `SubagentStop` hook fires when a subagent is about to stop.

### Input

In addition to the [common input](about:blank#_common-input), the hook receives:

```
{  "agent_id": "subagent-456",  "agent_type": "Plan",  "stop_hook_active": false}
```

| Field              | Type    | Description                                                                                       |

| Interactivity                   | Fully non-interactive. The agent runs with all tool permissions pre-granted, so no permission dialogs are shown and no notifications are surfaced to a user.                                                                                                                               |
| Configuration discovery         | In a cloud agent job, the only hook configuration that exists by default is `.github/hooks/*.json` inside the cloned repository. The sandbox does not ship with user-level hook files, `settings.json`, `config.json`, or installed plugins.                                               |

## Hook configuration format

Hook configuration files use JSON format with version `1`.

> \[!NOTE]
> If a hook configuration file loaded from a directory (for example, `.github/hooks/`) contains a malformed hook item, only that item is dropped and logged—valid sibling hooks in the same file still load. Structural errors (invalid JSON, a bad `version`, or a non-array event list) still reject the entire file. Hooks defined inline in `settings.json` remain strict: any item-level validation error rejects the whole `hooks` field. Other configuration files always load independently.

### Command hooks

Command hooks run shell scripts or executables and are supported on all hook types.

> \[!NOTE]
> **Cloud agent only.** Cloud agent runs hooks in a Linux sandbox. Only the `bash` field is honored; `powershell` entries are ignored. The cross-platform `command` field is honored as a fallback.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "hooks": {
    "preToolUse": [
      {
        "type": "command",
        "bash": "YOUR_BASH_COMMAND",
        "powershell": "YOUR_POWERSHELL_COMMAND",
        "cwd": "OPTIONAL/WORKING/DIRECTORY",
        "env": { "VAR": "VALUE" },
        "timeoutSec": 30
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

In Copilot CLI, you can use `exec` and `args` to run an executable directly instead of using a shell:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "hooks": {
    "p…[truncated]

echo '{"type": "progress", "message": "Routing...", "temporary": true}'
echo '{"type": "progress", "message": "Thinking...", "temporary": true}'
# ... perform work ...
echo '{"permissionDecision": "allow"}'
```

Progress messages are display-only and do not affect hook output or decision logic.

**How stdout is parsed when progress messages are mixed in.** — The CLI scans stdout line-by-line as the hook runs. Any line that, after trimming, is a single complete JSON object with `"type": "progress"` is consumed as a progress event and **removed from the hook's output stream**. Every other line—blank lines, plain text, and JSON objects that are not progress messages—is preserved verbatim. When the hook exits, the preserved lines are concatenated, trimmed, and parsed with a single `JSON.parse` call: that result is the hook's output (the "hook output JSON" referenced elsewhere in this article). This means:

* Emitting progress lines alongside a final decision object (as in the examples above) is safe and is the intended pattern—the progress lines never reach the JSON parser.
* Each progress message must be on its own line and must be valid JSON on that single line. Multi-line / pretty-printed progress objects are not recognized as progress and will be left in the output stream, where they will likely cause the final `JSON.parse` to fail.
* The final decision object, by contrast, may span multiple lines—only progress *recognition* is line-oriented; what remains after progress stripping is parsed as one JSON document, not as line-delimited JSON.
* If the leftover output is empty, or fails to parse as JSON, the hook is treated as having produced no output and falls through to default behavior. Two or more non-progress JSON objects on stdout (for example, two `echo '{"permissionDecision": ...}'` calls) will therefore concatenate into invalid JSON and be ignored—emit exactly one final decision object.

# Project conventions for AI agents

Invoice approval demo app: ASP.NET Core 8 Web API with a small static web UI.

## Layout

- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Domain`: business rules, no web or storage code. `ApprovalService` owns the invoice lifecycle (Draft, PendingApproval, Approved, Rejected).
- Approval-limit rules live in Domain (`ApprovalService` or a dedicated policy class). The API gets the approver's role from the session and passes it into Domain; Domain must never read HTTP or session state.
- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api`: controllers, sign-in (`Auth/`), in-memory repository, and the web UI under `wwwroot/`.
- `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`: xUnit tests, one test class per class under test, named `<ClassUnderTest>Tests`.
- `e2e`: Playwright end-to-end tests (`tests/`) and page objects (`pages/`).
- `docs/use-cases`: short briefs for features we may build.

## Approval limits (feature on branch feature/approval-limits)

- Only Manager and Director may approve; Admin retains admin rights but cannot approve.
- Manager may approve up to and including 50,000.00. Director may approve alone up to and including 500,000.00.
- Above 500,000.00 requires two distinct approvers: the first may be a Manager or Director; the second must be a Director.
- Negative rule 1: the same user can never count as both approvers; compare usernames case-insensitively.
- Negative rule 2: a blocked attempt must return a clear reason and change nothing: no status, approver, first approval, timestamp, or repository `Update` call. Throw a dedicated Domain exception; `ApiControllerBase` maps it to 403 Forbidden.
- Amounts are `decimal`; never use `float` or `double` for money.
- Repositories return the same object reference from `GetById`, and `FakeInvoiceRepository.Update` is a no-op. Validate everything before mutating; snapshot every invoice field in blocked-attempt tests and assert none changed.

# Invoice Approval Demo App

A small invoice approval app used for live AI-in-SDLC demos. It is deliberately simple: a .NET 8 API, a plain web UI, and an in-memory store, so it runs with one command and no database.

## Run it

```
dotnet run --project backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api
```

Open http://localhost:5000 and sign in:

| User | Password | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `demo.approver` | `ChangeMe123!` | Approver |
| `demo.admin` | `ChangeMe123!` | Admin |

These are demo accounts for a local, in-memory app. They are not real credentials.

## What it does

1. Create an invoice (it starts as a draft).
2. Submit it for approval.
3. An approver approves it, or rejects it with a reason.

Invoices move through Draft, Pending Approval, then Approved or Rejected.

## Tests

```
dotnet test backend/InvoiceApp.sln
```

## Project layout

```
backend/
  src/InvoiceApp.Domain   business rules
  src/InvoiceApp.Api      controllers, sign-in, web UI (wwwroot)
  tests/InvoiceApp.Tests  xUnit tests
docs/use-cases            short feature briefs
AGENTS.md                 conventions for AI coding agents
```

## Use cases

- [UC-1 Bulk invoice approval](docs/use-cases/UC-1-bulk-approval.md)
- [UC-2 Partial approval](docs/use-cases/UC-2-partial-approval.md)

# Project conventions for AI agents

Invoice approval demo app: ASP.NET Core 8 Web API with a small static web UI.

## Layout

- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Domain`: business rules, no web or storage code. `ApprovalService` owns the invoice lifecycle (Draft, PendingApproval, Approved, Rejected).

# Invoice Approval Demo App

A small invoice approval app used for live AI-in-SDLC demos. It is deliberately simple: a .NET 8 API, a plain web UI, and an in-memory store, so it runs with one command and no database.

## Run it

```
dotnet run --project backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api
```

Open http://localhost:5000 and sign in:

| User | Password | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `demo.approver` | `ChangeMe123!` | Approver |
| `demo.admin` | `ChangeMe123!` | Admin |

These are demo accounts for a local, in-memory app. They are not real credentials.

## What it does

1. Create an invoice (it starts as a draft).
2. Submit it for approval.
3. An approver approves it, or rejects it with a reason.

Invoices move through Draft, Pending Approval, then Approved or Rejected.

## Tests

```
dotnet test backend/InvoiceApp.sln
```

## Project layout

```
backend/
  src/InvoiceApp.Domain   business rules
  src/InvoiceApp.Api      controllers, sign-in, web UI (wwwroot)
  tests/InvoiceApp.Tests  xUnit tests
docs/use-cases            short feature briefs
AGENTS.md                 conventions for AI coding agents
```

## Use cases

- [UC-1 Bulk invoice approval](docs/use-cases/UC-1-bulk-approval.md)
- [UC-2 Partial approval](docs/use-cases/UC-2-partial-approval.md)

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Defines who may approve invoices at each amount and when high-value invoices require a second approver, while making blocked attempts explicit and non-mutating.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Approval authority follows role and amount limits
The system SHALL allow only Managers and Directors to approve invoices, subject to their individual amount limits.

#### Scenario: Manager approves at the inclusive limit
- **WHEN** a Manager approves an invoice for 50,000.00
- **THEN** the invoice becomes Approved with that Manager recorded as the approver

#### Scenario: Manager is blocked above the limit
- **WHEN** a Manager attempts to approve an invoice for 50,000.01 as a single approver
- **THEN** the attempt is blocked with reason `Manager may approve invoices up to 50,000.00.`

#### Scenario: Director approves at the inclusive single-approval limit
- **WHEN** a Director approves an invoice for 500,000.00
- **THEN** the invoice becomes Approved with that Director recorded as the approver

#### Scenario: Admin cannot approve
- **WHEN** an Admin attempts to approve an invoice at any amount
- **THEN** the attempt is blocked with reason `Only Manager or Director may approve invoices.`

#### Scenario: Other roles cannot approve
- **WHEN** a user whose role is neither Manager nor Director attempts to approve an invoice
- **THEN** the attempt is blocked with reason `Only Manager or Director may approve invoices.`

### Requirement: High-value invoices require two approvals
An invoice above 500,000.00 SHALL remain pending after an eligible first approval and become approved only after a Director gives a second approval.

#### Scenario: Invoice at the single-approval boundary needs no second approver
- **WHEN** a Director approves an invoice for 500,000.00
- **THEN** the invoice becomes Approved in that single approval

#### Scenario: Manager gives the first approval above the boundary
- **WHEN** a Manager a…[truncated]

# Proposal

## Why

The current approval flow lets any approver decide an invoice alone, regardless of amount. Role-based thresholds and a two-person rule for high-value invoices make approval authority explicit while preserving the existing invoice lifecycle and returning actionable explanations for blocked attempts.

## What Changes

- Replace the single-approver rule with Manager and Director approval limits: Manager through 50,000.00 and Director alone through 500,000.00.
- Require a Manager or Director as the first approver above 500,000.00 and a different Director as the second approver; keep the invoice pending and record the first approver between approvals.
- Block Admin and other roles from approving, without changing any invoice state or calling repository `Update`; return a dedicated Domain exception mapped to HTTP 403 with `{ "error": reason }`.
- Replace the `demo.approver` account with `demo.manager`, add `demo.director` and `demo.director2`, and retain `demo.admin`, all with the existing demo-only password.
- Add focused Domain unit tests, an over-limit rejection Playwright test, mutation-test score recording, and an agent review stage.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `invoice-approval`: Role- and amount-based approval eligibility, multi-approver completion for high-value invoices, and unchanged-state behavior for blocked attempts.

### Modified Capabilities

None.

## Impact

- Domain: approval service, invoice approval metadata, and a dedicated blocked-approval exception.
- API: approval controller role attributes and role forwarding; shared controller error mapping; demo-user configuration and README account list.
- Tests: approval-service unit tests and repository update-call tracking; one Playwright UI test using the relevant page objects and role-based locators.
- Validation: .NET tests, E2E test, Stryker baseline/after scores, and an agent review. No persistence changes or new dependencies are intended.

# Project conventions for AI agents

Invoice approval demo app: ASP.NET Core 8 Web API with a small static web UI.

## Layout

- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Domain`: business rules, no web or storage code. `ApprovalService` owns the invoice lifecycle (Draft, PendingApproval, Approved, Rejected).
- Approval-limit rules live in Domain (`ApprovalService` or a dedicated policy class). The API gets the approver's role from the session and passes it into Domain; Domain must never read HTTP or session state.
- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api`: controllers, sign-in (`Auth/`), in-memory repository, and the web UI under `wwwroot/`.
- `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`: xUnit tests, one test class per class under test, named `<ClassUnderTest>Tests`.
- `e2e`: Playwright end-to-end tests (`tests/`) and page objects (`pages/`).
- `docs/use-cases`: short briefs for features we may build.

## Approval limits (feature on branch feature/approval-limits)

- Only Manager and Director may approve; Admin retains admin rights but cannot approve.
- Manager may approve up to and including 50,000.00. Director may approve alone up to and including 500,000.00.
- Above 500,000.00 requires two distinct approvers: the first may be a Manager or Director; the second must be a Director.
- Negative rule 1: the same user can never count as both approvers; compare usernames case-insensitively.
- Negative rule 2: a blocked attempt must return a clear reason and change nothing: no status, approver, first approval, timestamp, or repository `Update` call. Throw a dedicated Domain exception; `ApiControllerBase` maps it to 403 Forbidden.
- Amounts are `decimal`; never use `float` or `double` for money.
- Repositories return the same object reference from `GetById`, and `FakeInvoiceRepository.Update` is a no-op. Validate everything before mutating; snapshot every invoice field in blocked-attempt tests and assert none changed.

# Mutation testing

## When to use

- You need to measure whether tests detect changes to production behavior.
- Approval-rule tests have changed and their effectiveness needs checking.

## Procedure

1. If the global tool is not installed, install the required version: `dotnet tool install -g dotnet-stryker --version 4.13.0`.

# Project conventions for AI agents

Invoice approval demo app: ASP.NET Core 8 Web API with a small static web UI.

## Layout

- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Domain`: business rules, no web or storage code. `ApprovalService` owns the invoice lifecycle (Draft, PendingApproval, Approved, Rejected).

# Design

## Context

See [proposal.md](./proposal.md) for motivation and [specs/invoice-approval/spec.md](./specs/invoice-approval/spec.md) for the behavior contract. `ApprovalService` currently performs a single approval by changing `Status`, `DecidedBy`, and `DecidedAt` before calling `IInvoiceRepository.Update`. The authenticated session provides both username and role, but the approval controller currently passes only the username. `ApiControllerBase.Handle` maps standard exceptions, while the UI already displays an API response's `error` property. Unit tests use a same-reference fake repository whose `Update` is currently a no-op.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**
- Keep approval eligibility and workflow transitions in Domain, with role and username supplied by the API.
- Ensure all validation completes before any invoice field is changed or `Update` is called.
- Preserve `DecidedBy` and `DecidedAt` as the final decision fields, and retain first-approval attribution for the high-value two-step path.
- Verify behavior and repository interaction at the unit-test boundary, with a focused API mapping test and one UI E2E regression.

**Non-Goals:**
- Bulk or partial approvals, UI redesign, durable storage, or database migration.
- Changing rejection policy beyond ensuring the approval route's role changes do not accidentally broaden rejection access.

## Decisions

1. **Pass the authenticated role and username into the Domain approval operation.** The controller obtains both from `HttpContext.GetSession()`. Domain receives plain values and has no dependency on HTTP or session types. Avoid putting amount checks or approval decisions in the controller.

# Proposal

## Why

The current approval flow lets any approver decide an invoice alone, regardless of amount. Role-based thresholds and a two-person rule for high-value invoices make approval authority explicit while preserving the existing invoice lifecycle and returning actionable explanations for blocked attempts.

## What Changes

- Replace the single-approver rule with Manager and Director approval limits: Manager through 50,000.00 and Director alone through 500,000.00.
- Require a Manager or Director as the first approver above 500,000.00 and a different Director as the second approver; keep the invoice pending and record the first approver between approvals.
- Block Admin and other roles from approving, without changing any invoice state or calling repository `Update`; return a dedicated Domain exception mapped to HTTP 403 with `{ "error": reason }`.
- Replace the `demo.approver` account with `demo.manager`, add `demo.director` and `demo.director2`, and retain `demo.admin`, all with the existing demo-only password.
- Add focused Domain unit tests, an over-limit rejection Playwright test, mutation-test score recording, and an agent review stage.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `invoice-approval`: Role- and amount-based approval eligibility, multi-approver completion for high-value invoices, and unchanged-state behavior for blocked attempts.

### Modified Capabilities

None.

## Impact

- Domain: approval service, invoice approval metadata, and a dedicated blocked-approval exception.
- API: approval controller role attributes and role forwarding; shared controller error mapping; demo-user configuration and README account list.
- Tests: approval-service unit tests and repository update-call tracking; one Playwright UI test using the relevant page objects and role-based locators.
- Validation: .NET tests, E2E test, Stryker baseline/after scores, and an agent review. No persistence changes or new dependencies are intended.

## Purpose

Defines who may approve invoices at each amount and when high-value invoices require a second approver, while making blocked attempts explicit and non-mutating.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Approval authority follows role and amount limits
The system SHALL allow only Managers and Directors to approve invoices, subject to their individual amount limits.

#### Scenario: Manager approves at the inclusive limit
- **WHEN** a Manager approves an invoice for 50,000.00

- **WHEN** a Manager attempts to approve an invoice for 500,000.00

#### Scenario: Director approves at the inclusive single-approval limit
- **WHEN** a Director approves an invoice for 500,000.00

- **WHEN** an Admin attempts to approve an invoice at any amount

# Invoice Approval Demo App

A small invoice approval app used for live AI-in-SDLC demos. It is deliberately simple: a .NET 8 API, a plain web UI, and an in-memory store, so it runs with one command and no database.

## Run it

```
dotnet run --project backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api
```

Open http://localhost:5000 and sign in:

| User | Password | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `demo.approver` | `ChangeMe123!` | Approver |
| `demo.admin` | `ChangeMe123!` | Admin |

These are demo accounts for a local, in-memory app. They are not real credentials.

## What it does

1. Create an invoice (it starts as a draft).
2. Submit it for approval.
3. An approver approves it, or rejects it with a reason.

Invoices move through Draft, Pending Approval, then Approved or Rejected.

## Tests

```
dotnet test backend/InvoiceApp.sln
```

## Project layout

```
backend/
  src/InvoiceApp.Domain   business rules
  src/InvoiceApp.Api      controllers, sign-in, web UI (wwwroot)
  tests/InvoiceApp.Tests  xUnit tests
docs/use-cases            short feature briefs
AGENTS.md                 conventions for AI coding agents
```

## Use cases

- [UC-1 Bulk invoice approval](docs/use-cases/UC-1-bulk-approval.md)
- [UC-2 Partial approval](docs/use-cases/UC-2-partial-approval.md)

See [proposal.md](./proposal.md) for motivation and [specs/invoice-approval/spec.md](./specs/invoice-approval/spec.md) for the behavior contract. `ApprovalService` currently performs a single approval by changing `Status`, `DecidedBy`, and `DecidedAt` before calling `IInvoiceRepository.Update`. - Keep approval eligibility and workflow transitions in Domain, with role and username supplied by the API.

- Preserve `DecidedBy` and `DecidedAt` as the final decision fields, and retain first-approval attribution for the high-value two-step path.
- Verify behavior and repository interaction at the unit-test boundary, with a focused API mapping test and one UI E2E regression.

- Bulk or partial approvals, UI redesign, durable storage, or database migration.

- A Domain approval rule is added, changed, or needs stronger regression coverage.

1. Add tests in `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests/ApprovalServiceTests.cs`. Name each test after the rule it proves; use one test per rule.
2. For each threshold or eligibility condition, test a boundary pair: an allowed value and the adjacent blocked value.
3. For **every** blocked case, assert the exact reason, snapshot **all** invoice fields before the attempt, and assert every field is unchanged afterward. Also assert `FakeInvoiceRepository.Update` was called zero times.
4. Use the pattern in [blocked-attempt-test-template.cs](./assets/blocked-attempt-test-template.cs); include every field from the current `Invoice` model in the snapshot.

After a blocked same-user second approval, assert the first approval is still recorded unchanged and that a different Director can still complete the approval.
6. Assert concrete outcomes and reasons. Never write a test that only asserts “no exception.”
7. Run `dotnet test backend/InvoiceApp.sln` and confirm the new tests pass.

# Project conventions for AI agents

Invoice approval demo app: ASP.NET Core 8 Web API with a small static web UI.

## Layout

- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Domain`: business rules, no web or storage code. `ApprovalService` owns the invoice lifecycle (Draft, PendingApproval, Approved, Rejected).
- Approval-limit rules live in Domain (`ApprovalService` or a dedicated policy class). The API gets the approver's role from the session and passes it into Domain; Domain must never read HTTP or session state.
- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api`: controllers, sign-in (`Auth/`), in-memory repository, and the web UI under `wwwroot/`.
- `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`: xUnit tests, one test class per class under test, named `<ClassUnderTest>Tests`.
- `e2e`: Playwright end-to-end tests (`tests/`) and page objects (`pages/`).
- `docs/use-cases`: short briefs for features we may build.

## Approval limits (feature on branch feature/approval-limits)

- Only Manager and Director may approve; Admin retains admin rights but cannot approve.
- Manager may approve up to and including 50,000.00. Director may approve alone up to and including 500,000.00.
- Above 500,000.00 requires two distinct approvers: the first may be a Manager or Director; the second must be a Director.
- Negative rule 1: the same user can never count as both approvers; compare usernames case-insensitively.
- Negative rule 2: a blocked attempt must return a clear reason and change nothing: no status, approver, first approval, timestamp, or repository `Update` call. Throw a dedicated Domain exception; `ApiControllerBase` maps it to 403 Forbidden.

# Design

## Context

See [proposal.md](./proposal.md) for motivation and [specs/invoice-approval/spec.md](./specs/invoice-approval/spec.md) for the behavior contract. `ApprovalService` currently performs a single approval by changing `Status`, `DecidedBy`, and `DecidedAt` before calling `IInvoiceRepository.Update`. The authenticated session provides both username and role, but the approval controller currently passes only the username. `ApiControllerBase.Handle` maps standard exceptions, while the UI already displays an API response's `error` property. Unit tests use a same-reference fake repository whose `Update` is currently a no-op.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**
- Keep approval eligibility and workflow transitions in Domain, with role and username supplied by the API.
- Ensure all validation completes before any invoice field is changed or `Update` is called.
- Preserve `DecidedBy` and `DecidedAt` as the final decision fields, and retain first-approval attribution for the high-value two-step path.
- Verify behavior and repository interaction at the unit-test boundary, with a focused API mapping test and one UI E2E regression.

**Non-Goals:**
- Bulk or partial approvals, UI redesign, durable storage, or database migration.
- Changing rejection policy beyond ensuring the approval route's role changes do not accidentally broaden rejection access.

1. **Pass the authenticated role and username into the Domain approval operation.** The controller obtains both from `HttpContext.GetSession()`. Domain receives plain values and has no dependency on HTTP or session types. Avoid putting amount checks or approval decisions in the controller.

# Project conventions for AI agents

Invoice approval demo app: ASP.NET Core 8 Web API with a small static web UI.

## Layout

- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Domain`: business rules, no web or storage code. `ApprovalService` owns the invoice lifecycle (Draft, PendingApproval, Approved, Rejected).
- Approval-limit rules live in Domain (`ApprovalService` or a dedicated policy class). The API gets the approver's role from the session and passes it into Domain; Domain must never read HTTP or session state.
- `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api`: controllers, sign-in (`Auth/`), in-memory repository, and the web UI under `wwwroot/`.
- `backend/tests/InvoiceApp.Tests`: xUnit tests, one test class per class under test, named `<ClassUnderTest>Tests`.
- `e2e`: Playwright end-to-end tests (`tests/`) and page objects (`pages/`).
- `docs/use-cases`: short briefs for features we may build.

## Approval limits (feature on branch feature/approval-limits)

- Only Manager and Director may approve; Admin retains admin rights but cannot approve.
- Manager may approve up to and including 50,000.00. Director may approve alone up to and including 500,000.00.
- Above 500,000.00 requires two distinct approvers: the first may be a Manager or Director; the second must be a Director.
- Negative rule 1: the same user can never count as both approvers; compare usernames case-insensitively.
- Negative rule 2: a blocked attempt must return a clear reason and change nothing: no status, approver, first approval, timestamp, or repository `Update` call. Throw a dedicated Domain exception; `ApiControllerBase` maps it to 403 Forbidden.
- Amounts are `decimal`; never use `float` or `double` for money.
- Repositories return the same object reference from `GetById`, and `FakeInvoiceRepository.Update` is a no-op. Validate everything before mutating; snapshot every invoice field in blocked-attempt tests and assert none changed.

description: Add or change invoice approval rules in InvoiceApp.Domain. Use when implementing approval limits, approver roles, or approval eligibility; keep business rules out of API controllers and preserve the single source of truth in AGENTS.md.

# Add an approval rule

## When to use

- A request adds or changes who may approve an invoice, or under what conditions.
- An existing approval decision needs a new validation rule.

For the authoritative limits and approval constraints, see [AGENTS.md — Approval limits](../../../AGENTS.md#approval-limits). Do not duplicate those rules here.

## Procedure

1. Read [AGENTS.md — Approval limits](../../../AGENTS.md#approval-limits) and inspect `ApprovalService` in `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Domain`.
2. Keep the rule in Domain. Ensure the API obtains the approver's role from the authenticated session and passes it into Domain; Domain must not read HTTP or session state.
3. Validate **all** applicable conditions before changing any invoice field. Blocked attempts must leave the invoice unchanged and must not call repository `Update`.
4. For a blocked approval, throw the dedicated Domain exception with a clear reason. Confirm `ApiControllerBase` maps that exception to HTTP 403.
5. Add or update tests for the rule, including blocked behavior and unchanged invoice state. Follow [AGENTS.md — Testing expectations](../../../AGENTS.md#testing-expectations).
6. When adding roles or demo users, update the Demo accounts section in `AGENTS.md` and `Users` in `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api/appsettings.json`.
7. Run `dotnet build backend/InvoiceApp.sln` and `dotnet test backend/InvoiceApp.sln`.

## Done when

- [ ] The approval rule is implemented in Domain and uses the role passed from the API session.
- [ ] All validation precedes mutation; blocked attempts give a clear Domain exception and map to 403.

# Proposal

## Why

The current approval flow lets any approver decide an invoice alone, regardless of amount. Role-based thresholds and a two-person rule for high-value invoices make approval authority explicit while preserving the existing invoice lifecycle and returning actionable explanations for blocked attempts.

## What Changes

- Replace the single-approver rule with Manager and Director approval limits: Manager through 50,000.00 and Director alone through 500,000.00.
- Require a Manager or Director as the first approver above 500,000.00 and a different Director as the second approver; keep the invoice pending and record the first approver between approvals.
- Block Admin and other roles from approving, without changing any invoice state or calling repository `Update`; return a dedicated Domain exception mapped to HTTP 403 with `{ "error": reason }`.
- Replace the `demo.approver` account with `demo.manager`, add `demo.director` and `demo.director2`, and retain `demo.admin`, all with the existing demo-only password.
- Add focused Domain unit tests, an over-limit rejection Playwright test, mutation-test score recording, and an agent review stage.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `invoice-approval`: Role- and amount-based approval eligibility, multi-approver completion for high-value invoices, and unchanged-state behavior for blocked attempts.

### Modified Capabilities

None.

## Impact

- Domain: approval service, invoice approval metadata, and a dedicated blocked-approval exception.
- API: approval controller role attributes and role forwarding; shared controller error mapping; demo-user configuration and README account list.
- Tests: approval-service unit tests and repository update-call tracking; one Playwright UI test using the relevant page objects and role-based locators.
- Validation: .NET tests, E2E test, Stryker baseline/after scores, and an agent review. No persistence changes or new dependencies are intended.

# Design

## Context

See [proposal.md](./proposal.md) for motivation and [specs/invoice-approval/spec.md](./specs/invoice-approval/spec.md) for the behavior contract. `ApprovalService` currently performs a single approval by changing `Status`, `DecidedBy`, and `DecidedAt` before calling `IInvoiceRepository.Update`. The authenticated session provides both username and role, but the approval controller currently passes only the username. `ApiControllerBase.Handle` maps standard exceptions, while the UI already displays an API response's `error` property. Unit tests use a same-reference fake repository whose `Update` is currently a no-op.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**
- Keep approval eligibility and workflow transitions in Domain, with role and username supplied by the API.
- Ensure all validation completes before any invoice field is changed or `Update` is called.
- Preserve `DecidedBy` and `DecidedAt` as the final decision fields, and retain first-approval attribution for the high-value two-step path.
- Verify behavior and repository interaction at the unit-test boundary, with a focused API mapping test and one UI E2E regression.

**Non-Goals:**
- Bulk or partial approvals, UI redesign, durable storage, or database migration.
- Changing rejection policy beyond ensuring the approval route's role changes do not accidentally broaden rejection access.

1. **Pass the authenticated role and username into the Domain approval operation.** The controller obtains both from `HttpContext.GetSession()`. Domain receives plain values and has no dependency on HTTP or session types. Avoid putting amount checks or approval decisions in the controller.

Invoice approval demo app: ASP.NET Core 8 Web API with a small static web UI.

## Layout

# Add an approval rule

## When to use

- A request adds or changes who may approve an invoice, or under what conditions.
- An existing approval decision needs a new validation rule.

For the authoritative limits and approval constraints, see [AGENTS.md — Approval limits](../../../AGENTS.md#approval-limits). Do not duplicate those rules here.

## Procedure

1. Read [AGENTS.md — Approval limits](../../../AGENTS.md#approval-limits) and inspect `ApprovalService` in `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Domain`.
2. Keep the rule in Domain. Ensure the API obtains the approver's role from the authenticated session and passes it into Domain; Domain must not read HTTP or session state.
3. Validate **all** applicable conditions before changing any invoice field. Blocked attempts must leave the invoice unchanged and must not call repository `Update`.
4. For a blocked approval, throw the dedicated Domain exception with a clear reason. Confirm `ApiControllerBase` maps that exception to HTTP 403.
5. Add or update tests for the rule, including blocked behavior and unchanged invoice state. Follow [AGENTS.md — Testing expectations](../../../AGENTS.md#testing-expectations).
6. When adding roles or demo users, update the Demo accounts section in `AGENTS.md` and `Users` in `backend/src/InvoiceApp.Api/appsettings.json`.
7. Run `dotnet build backend/InvoiceApp.sln` and `dotnet test backend/InvoiceApp.sln`.

## Done when

- [ ] The approval rule is implemented in Domain and uses the role passed from the API session.
- [ ] All validation precedes mutation; blocked attempts give a clear Domain exception and map to 403.
- [ ] Related tests and any required demo-account updates are complete.
- [ ] Th…[truncated]

(5) same username as the first approver, compared case-insensitively → "A different user must give the second approval.";
    otherwise set Approved, DecidedBy, DecidedAt, keep FirstApprovedBy/FirstApprovedAt, Update called once.
    A blocked attempt never records, clears or changes the first approval. No UI changes in Stage 2.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Role checks in a filter could hide the required rejection reason] → Route authenticated approval attempts through Domain; use a dedicated exception mapping for eligibility blocks.
- [Mutating the same invoice reference before validation would make rejected attempts observable even without a repository write] → Complete all checks before touching any invoice property; snapshot every model field and assert no `Update` call in tests.
- [The Manager limit and Manager-first high-value path could be misread as conflicting] → Keep them distinct in the service decision order and tests: Manager cannot decide an invoice alone above 50,000.00, but may be the recorded first approver above 500,000.00.
- [Changing the controller's class-level role filter could broaden rejection access] → Add explicit role restriction at the reject action and cover the desired behavior while updating approval access.
- [A new API project reference for mapping tests may couple the Domain-focused unit test project to the host] → Keep the mapping assertion narrowly scoped to the controller result; introduce a separate API test project only if the existing test structure cannot support that seam cleanly.

## Migration Plan

This demo uses an in-memory repository, so no data migration or persistence rollback is needed. Deploy the application and configuration together; replace the old demo approver login in documentation and seeded attribution. Roll back by reverting the feature commits and restoring the old demo account configuration.
